verdict.rationale: Svelte ships its own AI tooling: an official MCP server whose `svelte-autofixer` tool statically analyses agent-generated code and returns issues and suggestions. Separately, `sv check` surfaces JavaScript/TypeScript compiler errors. However, nothing shows the autofixer targets type errors specifically, or that it resolves them itself rather than handing suggestions back to the agent. missing for 10: evidence the AI tooling consumes type-system/`sv check` errors, automatic resolution (not just suggestions) of TypeScript errors, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native developer, I can use AI tooling that automatically resolves type errors surfaced by the framework's type system

citations.quote: svelte-autofixer: Analyzes Svelte code and returns issues and suggestions.
The Svelte MCP (Model Context Protocol) server can help your agent write better Svelte code. It works by providing relevant documentation, and statically analysing generated code
`sv check` finds errors and warnings in your project, such as: unused CSS, accessibility hints, JavaScript/TypeScript compiler errors
